articles.title: Mancini refers to ‘double’ Manchester City contract and says it ‘isn’t my problem’
articles.summary: Coach alleged to have been paid for advisory work. Mancini says City ‘not guilty’ after Premier League ruling. Roberto Mancini appeared to acknowledge he had “a double contract” when he managed Manchester City after the club were found guilty of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules.
body: But Mancini, who in 2011-12 coached City to their first Premier League title in a half century and is now in charge of Italy, also said that what is developing potentially into the biggest scandal in English football history was “not a problem that concerns me”.

Among the raft of charges that City faced is an alleged failure to provide accurate details for player and manager payments between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons. The German magazine Der Spiegel in 2018 published evidence showing that Mancini doubled his base salary of £1.45m for advising a club in Abu Dhabi.

Mancini led City to their first titles after Abu Dhabi’s ruling family bought the club in 2008, also winning the FA Cup in 2011. He was fired by City days after a shocking loss to Wigan in the FA Cup final in 2013.
Mancini was asked about his contract with City at Italy’s news conference in Turkey before a Nations League match on Monday.
points: Mancini says City ‘not guilty’ after Premier League ruling.

articles.title: FAI unclear over possible sanctions if game not played
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland could have faced 'undetermined' sanctions had they not played their Nations League match against Israel on Sunday, according to FAI president Paul Cooke.
body: Ireland and Israel players did not shake hands and the Irish squad bowed their heads when Israel's anthem was played before their 3-0 win in Hungary.
The two Nations League fixtures, being played at neutral venues, have been embroiled in controversy since February when the two teams were drawn to play each other in Group B3.

The Republic of Ireland players have faced calls to withdraw from the games because of the ongoing Israel-Gaza war with a "Stop The Game" campaign - organised by the pressure group Irish Sport for Palestine - gathering pace.
There was also no exchange of pennants between Republic of Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel skipper Manor Solomon, who did not shake hands.

articles.title: OK, now it’s time for the Patriots to panic about Drake Maye
articles.summary: The New England quarterback was a revelation in the 2025 regular season. But Sunday’s loss was just the latest in a series of crushing lows. After the Patriots pulled out a win in Week 2 over the Steelers, despite another uninspiring performance from Drake Maye, Mike Vrabel avoided answering…
body: On Sunday, Maye was largely responsible for ruining Vrabel’s afternoon in the Patriots’ 35-6 loss to Jacksonville, which felt like rock bottom (the Pats hope). Simply put, Maye was atrocious. The 2025 MVP runner-up was 14-of-25 for 199 yards, no touchdowns, two interceptions, three sacks, and a lost fumble.

It wasn’t just that Maye was once again a turnover machine – it was the weirdness of his decision making. A particularly grievous error came on a third and goal with under a minute remaining in the first half. New England were only down 14-3 and well-positioned to shift the game’s momentum. Then Maye threw the ball right to Jacksonville corner Travis Hunter in the end zone.

It’s hard to comprehend what Maye was seeing or not seeing on that play. Given the ball placement and defensive reads, some social-media jokesters questioned whether he could even make out Jacksonville’s teal uniforms.

articles.title: Data shows England made inroads against Spain but they must be more clinical | Andrew Beasley
articles.summary: Thomas Tuchel’s side had 36 touches in the Spain penalty area at Wembley but were given a lesson in taking chances. England dominated Spain to an extent very few teams have in recent years. Sadly for them, not in terms of goals. Nor possession.
body: They allowed just 9.5 touches per 90 minutes at the 2026 World Cup. The combined efforts of Belgium, France and Argentina registered 38 touches in the Spain box in the final three rounds of the tournament. Since available records began (at the start of Euro 2016), the most box touches a side has had against Spain was the 45 Germany had in the quarter-final of Euro 2024. However, that game went to extra time. France had 42 in normal time in the ridiculous Nations League semi-final they lost 5-4 last year, then come England, second best in regular time from a sample of 133 matches.

Given they were so active in the penalty area, they should have created more. Germany generated 2.15 non-penalty expected goals in the above example, France 1.95 and England just 0.95. The latter averaged 5.1 box touches for each shot they had in the penalty area, or 5.8 without Harry Kane’s spot kick. Tottenham have been criticised for being inefficient in this regard this season and their average of 3.6 – the highest in the Premier League – is well below England’s level against Spain.

articles.title: The four 'what next?' scenarios for Premier League after Man City ruling
articles.summary: It has taken more than two years, but a judgement finally appears to have been made on the 115 charges levelled against Manchester City. Here's what it means.
body: If you were getting the impression that the saga over Manchester City 's 115 charges was almost over, think again.
Two years and 10 days since the hearing began, and 1,329 days after City were charged, we now know a verdict has been reached, with the club guilty of the majority of financial rule breaches.
BBC Sport was later told the verdict was sent during the week to club executives, who had to sign a non-disclosure agreement to open the file.
A process can appear to be completely watertight, as this one certainly had been, but when the circle of trust is expanded, the chance of information getting out increases.

articles.summary: Former England Test batter Tom Westley steps down as captain of Essex after seven seasons in the role.
body: Essex finished eighth in Division One of the County Championship, one spot above the relegation places.
However, their top-flight status rests on the outcome of Leicestershire's appeal against a 27-point deduction for breaching pitch regulations.

A draw against Glamorgan in their final match meant Essex ended the season 25 points clear of the Foxes, who will stay up at Essex's expense if their appeal is successful and they get all 27 points back.
Westley, Essex's longest-serving player, said captaining the county had been his "greatest honour".

articles.title: Referee Accused Of Bias Toward Patrick Mahomes After Controversial Chop Robinson Roughing Call
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes has spent most of his NFL career finding ways to stay calm when a play breaks down. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback has taken plenty of hits while extending plays, scrambling for extra yards and waiting for receivers to get open.
body: That has become part of playing the position in Kansas City. Mahomes entered Sunday’s game against the Miami Dolphins with the Chiefs unbeaten and coming off a strong start to the season, while Miami was still looking for its first win.

The Chiefs were holding a 14-10 lead late in the third quarter when Mahomes faced third-and-9 from his own 5-yard line. He dropped back and threw toward Rashee Rice, but Miami pass rusher Chop Robinson reached him just as the ball left his hand.

Robinson was called for roughing the passer. Miami was also flagged for defensive holding on the same play, meaning Kansas City would have received a first down either way, but the roughing penalty gave the Chiefs 15 additional yards. Kansas City eventually moved down the field and Harrison Butker made a 34-yard field goal to make it 17-10.
Mahomes did not blame Robinson for the hit. In fact, he gave the Dolphins pass rusher credit for making a good play.

articles.title: CBS’ Nate Burleson outlines what Travis Kelce did during the offseason to inspire early NFL season form
articles.summary: Former NFL wide receiver Nate Burleson has shared his theory behind Travis Kelce’s 2026 resurgence. The Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end has looked phenomenal through the first three games of the new season.
body: After seven consecutive seasons with more than 1,000 receiving yards, Kelce has failed to reach the same mark in each of the last three years. The 2025 season was arguably the least productive of his career, with 76 receptions for 851 yards in 17 starts.

However, Kelce appears to have returned to his old self in the first three games of the new campaign. He has recorded 231 receiving yards at a career-high average of 16.5 yards per reception, while also scoring two touchdowns during the Chiefs' 3-0 start.

Nate Burleson suggested that Travis Kelce's extremely busy 2025 offseason contributed to his down year with the Kansas City Chiefs. Kelce got engaged to global pop star Taylor Swift that summer and took part in several extracurricular activities, including television appearances.

The former Seattle Seahawks receiver claimed that Kelce was more focused on football this offseason and is already reaping the rewards. The 36-year-old currently has the second-most receiving yards among all tight ends in 2026, behind only the Buffalo Bills ' Dalton Kincaid.

articles.summary: Reigning Formula 1 world champion Lando Norris said he apologised to Franco Colapinto for the stinging comments he made after the Alpine driver caused a crash that took both of them out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
body: Colapinto triggered the accident during a Safety Car restart in Baku when he locked his brakes into the first corner and hit the side of his Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly, who was sent straight into Norris' McLaren on his outside.

Speaking in the immediate aftermath of the incident in Saturday's race, Norris said "there are some drivers who shouldn't be in Formula 1" and called for such incidents to result in one-race bans for the initiator.
Colapinto apologised to both Gasly and Norris during his post-race interviews, but the Argentine driver was handed a five-place grid penalty for this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
On Monday morning, Norris posted on Instagram: "Tough weekend overall in Baku and of course a disappointing and early end to the race.

articles.summary: The Florida Gators entered Week 4 with an amazing victory against No. 4 Ole Miss on Saturday. The organization dominated the game and won 52-28. Head coach Jon Sumrall was under immense pressure as both teams were ranked in the Top 25.
body: The head coach showed his excitement to the Florida fans and made sure the fans know that he is not interested in taking a slow approach to building the program.

“We’ve got a five-year plan too,” when asked about his five-month plan for the Gators this season. “We came here to win championships, but there’s no reason in the world that shouldn’t be the expectation at the University of Florida every year, so why wait? We’ve got a lot of good players. A lot of guys chose to stay and I’m not very patient. You can ask my wife.”
After their Saturday win, the organization is expected to make a significant jump in the new AP Poll, and there is much more room to climb with Texas and Georgia on the schedule later in the season.
“We’re still not a finished product, but the guys are giving great effort and they’re trying to do what we ask of them. We still didn’t play our best today.”

articles.title: Why Man City charges case could still drag on for years
articles.summary: Manchester City have been embroiled in legal disputes with UEFA and the Premier League for 12 years and they are so determined to clear their name, and the 115 charges case is so big, that it could still be years before the saga is concluded.
body: According to reports last week, an independent tribunal has reached decisions in the case and Sky Sports News understands that the process is moving to the appeal stage.

In 2014 City paid a £49m fine for breaking UEFA's financial fair play rules and in 2020 they were given a two-year European competition ban and fined €30m for breaking the rules again. The ban was overturned at the Court of Arbitration for Sport where City were cleared of disguising owner funding as sponsorship income.
That victory may give City fans hope that they can win again when their Premier League appeal is heard by a new three-person panel.
If the appeal goes against them, they will not be able to go to CAS but there is the strong possibility that City's owners would turn to the High Court to clear their name.

articles.title: Will Littler defend World Grand Prix title? Humphries, Price, Smith in the mix
articles.summary: Will Luke Littler successfully defend his World Grand Prix title? Can Luke Humphries, Gerwyn Price, James Wade or Ross Smith trouble the world No 1 in the unique double-in, double-out format?
body: Littler will be hoping the home crowd at Leicester's Mattioli Arena is more welcoming after the two-time world champion was booed and whistled at during the World Series of Darts Finals exit in Amsterdam earlier this month.

The 19-year-old headed into the tournament chasing a historic clean sweep after winning the first six major titles of the season but suffered a crushing 10-4 defeat to Jonny Clayton in the last eight.
Stephen Bunting backed Littler, saying he has "changed" darts since bursting onto the scene a few years ago.
"It's really hard, isn't it? Obviously, Luke is the best player in the world. For whatever reason, the crowd got on his back, they didn't want him to do the [clean sweep]," said Bunting.

videos.title: The advantages of being 5-foot-3
videos.summary: At 5-foot-3, how did Muggsy Bogues turn his height into an advantage — and build a 14-year NBA career?
body: Muggsy joins Ben Taylor of Thinking Basketball in our latest episode of "Anatomy of the Game" to reveal how he used timing, angles and his low center of gravity to thrive against much bigger opponents.

Together, they revisit his 18-point, 17-assist, 4-steal performance against the powerful duo of Penny Hardaway, Shaquille O’Neal and the eventual Eastern Conference champion Orlando Magic during the 1994–95 season but also revisit film of memorable matchups against Michael Jordan, Reggie Miller and more.

Muggsy explains how he picked elite ballhandlers’ pockets, held his ground against taller players in the post, deceived defenders with his eyes and attacked driving angles others simply couldn't access. Go inside the decisions and techniques that helped him not only make the NBA, but last in the league as a high-impact floor general and starter in his prime.
